ideas.title: A hand mirror, and friends who chase the sun spot
ideas.critique: A light the player steers and creatures that chase it is a real toy, and the island has never answered the player through light like this. The 'friends chase X' behaviour is close to the old sun-ball chase that never showed a chase, so the film has to show the pounce clearly. The traced spot and glint is strong material for goal 7.

ideas.title: Dominoes across the island
ideas.critique: The island already posted a domino chain laid by Lumi and tracked along the falling front, so the film would be the same recipe again. Player laying, real rigid bodies and stalls on slopes are a real step for play, but whoever watches the film gets the same payoff.

ideas.title: The owl that hunts by ear
ideas.critique: Binaural hearing traced through the acoustic ray tracer, with an owl fooled by a bounce off the cottage, gives the sound work its first actual gameplay and a stealth loop with real risk. It reuses the echo tracer the last two posts were about, but as a predator's ears, not one more film of the sound spreading out.

ideas.title: Glass blowing at the furnace
ideas.critique: A viscous shell solver that glows like a blackbody and cools to a dielectric with caustics is something the island never had, and it fits goal 7 directly. The worry is that a 1D profile shaped by holding keys plays like a lathe slider, and the payoff could end up as one more quiet still of a shelf.

ideas.title: Spinning tops on the cairn table
ideas.critique: Euler's equations with a top that rises from tip friction, precession and spin knocked out in clashes are real rigid body dynamics the island has never shown, and a short battle round is replayable. A battle-top game is a familiar genre, so the surprise depends on how visible the physics is in slow motion.

ideas.title: The morning paper
ideas.critique: Headlines ranked from the real event log turn play into news that lasts, which is a nice loop, but the planned film is a sheet blowing across the meadow, the third paper-falls short in a row. The front page is a layout over logs, and friends 'talking about it' tends to come out as one more round of one-liners.

ideas.title: Hide and seek in the dark, by clapping
same_form: The island answers a clap, a broken take
ideas.critique: It finally gives the clap a game, and friends creeping away from the sound is a good twist. But the film is again a night clap drawn as light, the third in a row, so a judge will see the same shape.

ideas.title: Reed duel at the pond
ideas.critique: Elastic rods with inertia and a grip that lets go above a force are real new motion, and a splash knock-out is a good payoff. Timing duels driven by rod physics often feel floaty and hard to read, and friend personalities can end up as random swinging.

ideas.title: The tide
ideas.critique: A sea level that follows the moon and leaves pools behind gives the island a rhythm, but it is one more island-wide change to the sea. The pools, crabs and things carried off are scripted pickups, not simulated water, and the timelapse is a predictable film.

ideas.title: Paper planes
ideas.critique: Throwing for distance is a fun skill game with a contest, but the film is again a PrintSim sheet gliding through air with the camera following it down, which is what the last two paper posts were. The glide needs a real pitching moment, or it will read as another slow fall.
